Load functions and packages

Load the packages and other functions that will be used during reorganisation.

source('HS_functions.R')

Load data

Load the raw data

Load the raw data exported from Excel to csv.

path_file = file.path("0Data",
                      c(
                        "H_calib.csv",#horizontal and dome calibrated dances 
                        "V_uncalib.csv"#vertical dances (not yet calibrated0)
                        )
)
if(any(!file.exists(path_file)))
{print(paste(path_file, '\nnot found'))}
hd = lapply(X = path_file,
            FUN = read.table,
                header = T, 
                sep  = ',')

Combine calibrated and uncalibrated data

Check that all column names match across files loaded.

nm_vert = names(hd[[1]])
nm_calib = names(hd[[2]])
if(any(!(nm_calib %in% nm_vert) |
       !(nm_vert %in% nm_calib))
   )
{
  message("horizontal columns not in vertical")
print(nm_calib[!(nm_calib %in% nm_vert)])
  message("vertical columns not in horizontal")
print(nm_vert[!(nm_vert %in% nm_calib)])
}else
{print("columns match in all CSVs")}
## [1] "columns match in all CSVs"

Bind the tables together one set of rows on top of the other

hd = do.call(what = rbind,
             args = hd)

Inspect data

Exported CSVs sometimes end up with empty rows at the end. Check that the last row contains data.

print(hd[dim(hd)[1],])

Rename variables

Rename some variables with shorter or easier to recognise names. Video names currently include the full path for the user that annotated them these can be simplified to just file name and folder (date recorded). There are two kinds of grouping factor, firstly the identity of the individual bee, simplified here to ID, and within each individual bee their individual dances, specified here as ID_d. The date is now in YYYYDDMM format, this will be reformatted later.

#from the list above, identify unused or renamed columns to remove
rm_lst = c(
  "recording_type", #not used currently
  "source_batch", #not used currently
  "dance_key", #not used currently
  "dance_id", #renamed
  "bee_id", # renamed
  "date", #renamed
  "time_dance", #renamed
  # [8,] "waggle_run"
  # [9,] "condition"
  "orientation_method", #not currently used
  # [11,] "csv_file"
  "video_name", #should be identifiable from video_file
  # [13,] "direction_u"
  # [14,] "direction_v"
  # [15,] "video_angle_deg"
  # [16,] "true_north_video_deg"
  # [17,] "waggle_true_bearing_deg"
  # [18,] "mean_magnetic_north_deg"
  # [19,] "true_north_calibration_deg"
  "compass_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  "calibration_n_annotations", #not currently used
  # [22,] "calibration_quality_flag"
  "reference_compass_file", #not currently used
  "assigned_calibration_file", #not currently used
  "calibration_id", #not currently used
  "calibration_file", #not currently used
  "reference_landmark_file", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_file", #not currently used
  "landmark_calibration_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_calibration_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  "north_relative_to_landmark_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_video_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  # [34,] "start_x"
  # [35,] "start_y"
  "start_xy", #same as start_x, start_y
  "start_frame", #not currently used
  "notes"
  # [39,] "calibration_R"
  # [40,] "declination_deg"
)
hd = within(hd, {
  ID = paste0(bee_id) # individual identifier
  ID_d = paste0(dance_id, "_", time_dance, "_", date) # dance identifier
  time = time_dance
  day = date # this will need to be converted to POSIX format

  video_file = file.path(
    basename(dirname(video_name)), #just the folder
    basename(video_name)
  ) # and file name
  #clean up information that has been doubled or will not be used
  rm(list = rm_lst)
})
#confirm resulting columns
names(hd)

Identify factor levels

Some of the character variables could be treated as factors. Inspect the different labels to each to check these are informative.

Click to expand full list 
nm_fact = c(
  # [1,] "waggle_run"
  "condition",
  # "csv_file", #easier to keep file paths as characters
  # [4,] "direction_u"
  # [5,] "direction_v"
  # [6,] "video_angle_deg"
  # [7,] "true_north_video_deg"
  # [8,] "waggle_true_bearing_deg"
  # [9,] "mean_magnetic_north_deg"
  # [10,] "true_north_calibration_deg"
  "calibration_quality_flag",
  # [12,] "start_x"
  # [13,] "start_y"
  # [14,] "calibration_R"
  # [15,] "declination_deg"
  # "video_file", #easier to keep file paths as characters
  # [17,] "day"
  # [18,] "time"
  "ID_d",
  "ID"
)
  
sapply(X = hd[, nm_fact],
       unique
     )

Add sun location

We can now use the time and date for each dance, combined with the location of the hive and feeder, to work out the relative positions of the hive, sun and feeder. This tells us what direction each dance should indicate for the feeder, as well as any potential effects of sun elevation on accuracy or skylight quality.

Check times and dates

                           subset = is.na(video_angle_deg) &

                    unique(ID_d)
                    )

            subset = !(ID_d %in% empty_dances)
            )

There is one empty dance that can be removed (possibly extra empty rows at end of CSV). A total of 4 dances have incomplete time or date, all of which are missing date currently. These seem to correspond to 4 videos, for which the date can be guessed from the folder name. It will now be possible to calculate sun azimuth for all remaining dances.

Set up times

First we need to combine dates in YYYYMMDD with times in HH:MM:SS to produce a POSIX/C99 “calendar time” for each. This is then converted to UTC for sun location estimation.

hd = within(hd,
            {
              time_code = mapply(FUN = paste, 
                                 day,
                                 time)#time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
              sast_time =  as.POSIXct(time_code, 
                                      tz = "Africa/Johannesburg", 
                                      format = "%Y%m%d %H:%M:%OS")#South African Standard time
                                      # format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS")#South African Standard time
              utc_time =  as.POSIXct(sast_time, tz = "UTC")#UTC time
              rm("time_code")#now duplicated
            }
)
with(hd, summary(utc_time))
##                  Min.               1st Qu.                Median 
## "2025-01-19 14:51:00" "2025-01-21 09:55:00" "2025-01-26 13:17:00" 
##                  Mean               3rd Qu.                  Max. 
## "2025-01-24 23:13:28" "2025-01-28 06:23:00" "2025-01-28 16:25:00"

In all cases time or date were available and could be converted, so it will be possible to calculate the sun’s azimuth for all of these.

Adjust for laptop clock (check this)

Videos recorded on the laptop have time stamps in CET not SAST. This means that they are one hour behind, since South African Summer time is UCT + 2, while Central European Winter is UTC + 1. Adjust them by adding one hour (60 minutes x 60 seconds) before calculating sun position.

hd = within(hd,
            {
              sast_time = as.POSIXct(
                mapply(FUN = switch,
                                 EXPR = condition,
                                 vertical = sast_time, # camcorder
                                 horizontal = sast_time, # camcorder
                                 deg_10 = sast_time,  # camcorder
                                 antisolar = sast_time + 60*60, #60 min x 60 seconds
                                 solar = sast_time + 60*60,
                                 zenith = sast_time + 60*60,
                                 sast_time
                                 ),
                tz = "Africa/Johannesburg", 
                format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS")#South African Standard time
              #recalculate UTC time
              utc_time =  as.POSIXct(sast_time, tz = "UTC")#UTC time
            }
            )

Estimate sun location

In order to determine the sun’s location (azimuth and elevation) we need to combine the time with the geographic location. GetSaz is a vectorised wrapper for oce::sunAngle, which corrects for refraction, but not the altitude from which the sun is viewed.

The current estimate of hive location is from a combination of Google Maps bookmarks and photograph metadata, cross-references with Google Earth satellite images.

# Hive position
# 25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E
#-25.57167,      31.18000 

hive = r"(25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E)" # N.B. this string contains literal " so needs wrapping in r"()"

# Define coordinates (lon, lat)
hive = Dms2decimal(hive) 

#add sun azimuth
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            sun_az = mapply(
                   FUN = GetSaz,
                   tm = utc_time,
                   lon = hive['longitude'],
                   lat = hive['latitude']
                   )
            }
            )

#add sun azimuth
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            sun_el = mapply(
                   FUN = GetSel,
                   tm = utc_time,
                   lon = hive['longitude'],
                   lat = hive['latitude']
                   )
            }
            )

print(with(hd, sapply(X = list(sun_az, sun_el),FUN =  summary)),
      digits = 2)
##          [,1] [,2]
## Min.      5.3   -8
## 1st Qu.  97.7   16
## Median  255.4   39
## Mean    218.1   40
## 3rd Qu. 266.3   70
## Max.    354.4   84

At the extremes we see Northerly azimuths (015°,340°), presumably around midday, while the most common sun azimuths are Westerly ($$270°) in the afternoon and evening. Solar elevations range between -8° (after sunset) and 84° (high noon). Around 25% are at high elevations (>75°).

Add Feeder angle

To determine the expected dance directions, we need to know the azimuth angle between the sun and the feeder, for which we need the bearing from the hive to the feeder. As for the hive position, the current estimate of feeder position was determined
from a combination of Google Maps bookmarks and photograph metadata, cross-referenced with Google Earth satellite images.

geosphere::bearing requires coordinates in decimal, with longitude first and then latitude, so Dms2decimal converts from degrees, minutes and seconds to decimal and reorders the (latitude,longitude) vector.

# Hive position
# 25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E
#-25.57167,      31.18000 

# Feeder position
# 25° 34' 14" S, 31° 10' 59" E
#-25.57056,      31.18306

hive = r"(25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E)" # N.B. this string contains literal " so needs wrapping in r"()"

feeder = r"(25° 34' 14" S, 31° 10' 59" E)"

# Define coordinates (lon, lat)
hive = Dms2decimal(hive) 
feeder =  Dms2decimal(feeder)
#N.B. Dms2decimal converts from (latitude, longitude) to (longitude, latitude)
# to conform with geosphere::bearing

# Calculate bearing from hive to feeder
feeder_bearing = bearing(hive, feeder)
print(feeder_bearing, digits = 3)
## [1] 68.2
feeder_distance = distGeo(hive, feeder)
print(feeder_distance, digits = 3)
## [1] 331
#add feeder azimuth relative to sun position
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            feeder_az = Mod360.180(feeder_bearing - sun_az)
            }
            )

print(with(hd, summary(feeder_az)), digits = 3)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  -177.1    53.1   161.6   115.9   172.6   179.9
print(with(hd, summary(abs(feeder_az))), digits = 3)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.113  55.096 161.629 122.975 172.573 179.916

Based on geographic position alone, we can conclude that the feeder was at a bearing of 068° (approx. East-North-East) from the hive, \(\approx\) 330m away. Given the hilly terrain, the ground distance flown may have been slightly further. After subtracting the sun’s azimuth, we see that the sun ranged between nearly 180° West of the feeder (presumably sunset) and precisely aligned with the feeder (presumably during the morning).

## -1.01e-12 -1.90e-13  1.40e-14  3.72e-14  2.91e-13  1.03e-12
#assign angles to numeric

#video_angle_deg is the dance angle clockwise rel to vertical, except  error
hd = within(hd, 
            {
              # bearing = deg(atan2(y = direction_v, x = direction_u) + pi/2) %% 360
              bearing = mapply(FUN = switch,
                               EXPR = condition,
                               horizontal = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #corrected with compass
                               deg10 = waggle_true_bearing_deg,
                               vertical =  video_angle_deg, #aligned by default
                               # antisolar = video_angle_deg, #aligned by default
                               # solar = (video_angle_deg +180) %% 360, #misaligned 180°
                               antisolar = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               solar = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               zenith = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               video_angle_deg
                              )
              signed_angle = Mod360.180(bearing)  # bearing between -180 and 180
              # angle = circular(rad(signed_angle),# bearing between -pi and pi
              #                  rotation = 'clock') # circular format suppresses later warnings
              angle = rad(signed_angle)# circular format is not needed for organising
                               
              rm('video_angle_deg')
            }
            )
with(hd, sapply(list(bearing, signed_angle, angle), FUN = summary))

## 3rd Qu. 231.85916   71.732387  1.2519663

Inspect dances

Plot an example dance

For example we can look at the dances for Blue-22 recorded on 2025-01-28 at 07:57:05, 08:10:00, 08:29:00, 08:34:00 & 10:44:09—each of which is the first for one of the conditions. Sun azimuth (possibly incorrect) is shown as an orange line.

subs_20250128 = subset(hd, day %in% "20250128")
#find first dance for each condition on 2025.01.28
example_lst = list()
for(stim in unique(hd$condition))
{
example_lst[[stim]] = with(subset(subs_20250128, condition %in% stim),
                           unique(ID_d)[1])
}
#inspect
print(t(t(unlist(example_lst))))

Calculate dance offset from feeder

#assign angles to numeric

#video_angle_deg is the dance angle clockwise rel to vertical, except  error
hd = within(hd, 
            {
              feeder_angle = mod_circular(rad(bearing - feeder_az))# angle between dance and expected dance
              abs_feeder_angle_deg = deg(abs(as.numeric(feeder_angle)))# absolute angle in numeric format
            }
            )

print(
  with(subset(hd, condition %in% 'vertical'), summary(abs_feeder_angle_deg)),
  digits = 2
)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.016   9.310  20.372  25.766  39.182 158.543
print(
  with(subset(hd, condition %in% 'horizontal'), summary(abs_feeder_angle_deg)),
  digits = 1
)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##     0.8    92.6   116.9   113.7   140.8   179.6

  with(subset(hd, condition %in% 'antisolar'), summary(abs_feeder_angle_deg)),
  digits = 1
)
